notes: DEFAULT: main passes &cfg, a frame record whose first member is a char *, to add and drop as a char **. add stores a node through it whose word stores would print one character at a time through a char *, and drop reads cfg->head past the first member, so neither takes char ** and both keep their one-field record; advance(&cursor) only reads and writes *cursor and takes char **. mkpipe hands p to pipe (int *) and keeps int * instead of a one-field record.
